messages.author: c9eb1b46bad3af54
messages.subject: Different scanone inputs same output
parts:
Hi, I am having some strange things happen with the rqtl outputs. I can change the inputs to calc.genoprob and the scanone method but I always get the same output. I am not sure how to fix it. Here is what I am running:

I can run one
sup2 <- calc.genoprob(data2, step=1)
sup4 <- calc.genoprob(data2, step=5)
sup6 <- calc.genoprob(data2, step=10)

then running scanone with any of these like so:

out <- scanone(sup2)

gives me the same output

Likewise running

out1 <- scanone(sup, method="hk")
or
out2 <- scanone(sup, method="ehk")

gives me the same output.

I also tried the imputation method on my data

sug8 <- sim.geno(data2, n.draws=100)
out.imp <-scanone(sug8, method="imp")

which also gave me the same output.

Any idea what is going on?

Thanks,
Emma

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Different scanone inputs same output
parts:
Try nrow(sup2) vs nrow(sup6). At the positions in common, the results should be the same, but they should differ in the density of positions at which the LOD scores were calculated.

Also try

plot(out1 - out2, ylim=c(-1, 1))

to see if there are subtle differences.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Different scanone inputs same output
parts:
Oops, sorry.

Rather than nrow(sup2) and nrow(sup6), try:

  sup2 <- calc.genoprob(data2, step=1)
  out.sup2 <- scanone(sup2)

  sup6 <- calc.genoprob(data2, step=10)
  out.sup6 <- scanone(sup6)

then nrow(out.sup2) and nrow(out.sup6).  Those should be different.

karl
